# Tombstone: turnstile double count as fare loss

Retired on 14 February 2031. The reading counted every turnstile rotation as a paid boarding, so double rotations looked like unpaid passengers. Replacement method: match each rotation to one scanned ticket. The remaining unmatched rotations were few and were explained by staff passes.

# Decision 0004: turnstile double count is not a fare loss vector

Accepted on 14 February 2031.

Turnstile double counts do not establish a ferry fare loss. Ticket-to-rotation matching is the retained method.

# Refund reversal analysis, 2 March 2031

As of 2 March 2031, the refund reversal mechanism remains open. Forty refunds were reversed after boarding and the cause is not yet known. Next step: trace the reversal job in the ticketing code.

---
id: kb-refund-reversal-closed
evidence: verifiable
provenance:
  - docs/analysis/2031-03-02-refund-reversal.md
  - docs/STATUS.md
---

# Refund reversal mechanism is closed

The refund reversal mechanism was closed on 9 March 2031 after the ticketing code trace confirmed that a retry job reversed refunds already served. It is not a fare loss vector. Only one narrower question remains open: whether refund reversals connect to the separate fare shortfall.

# Project status

## Refund reversal

Mechanism: closed on 9 March 2031; confirmed by the ticketing code trace; not a fare loss vector.

Still open: the possible connection between refund reversals and the fare shortfall.

## Fare shortfall

Open. The physical cause of the shortfall is not demonstrated.

This file records documentary status. It is not a live check of the ticketing system.

# Retired reading: duplicate checkout scans as stock loss

A replacement method now pairs every scan with one loan record; the handful of unpaired scans came from staff test cards. The old reading treated each scan as a separate loan. Retired 3 October 2033.

# ADR 0011 - duplicate scans do not explain missing stock

Pairing each scan with one loan record is the method we keep. Duplicate self-checkout scans do not establish missing library stock.

Accepted 3 October 2033.

# Hold expiry review, 21 October 2033

Twenty-six holds were released after the patron had already collected the book, and nobody knows why yet. On 21 October 2033 the hold expiry release mechanism is still open. Planned follow-up: read the nightly expiry job.

---
id: kb-hold-expiry-release-settled
evidence: verifiable
provenance:

  - docs/PROJECT-STATE.md
---

# Hold expiry release mechanism is settled

Whether hold expiry releases are linked to the unexplained shelf gap is the single question left open. The mechanism itself was settled on 30 October 2033: reading the nightly expiry job showed it released holds that had already been collected. It does not cause missing stock.

# Project state

These entries record documents only; nothing here is a live check of the lending system.

## Shelf gap

Open. Nobody has shown what physically causes the gap.

## Hold expiry release

Still open: whether hold expiry releases are linked to the shelf gap.

Mechanism: settled on 30 October 2033 by reading the nightly expiry job; not a cause of missing stock.
